\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بازنده} (bâzande)}{بازنده (bâzande)}]{\fa{بازنده} (bâzande) — a loser (of a game)}

\label{lesson:FA-C513-bazande}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a league, then the Persian for a point.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بازنده}}
\textbf{\fa{بازنده}} (\emph{bâzande}) — \textquotedblleft{}a loser (of a game)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بازنده} \fa{بازی} \fa{با} \fa{لبخند} \fa{دست} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bâzande-ye bâzi bâ labkhand dast dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The loser of the match shook hands with a smile.
\end{quote}

From \emph{bâz-}, the present stem of \emph{bâkhtan} 'to lose (a game)', + \emph{-ande} 'one who'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâzande} is built on native Persian \emph{bâz-}, the present stem of \emph{bâkhtan}, 'to lose a game', with the ending \emph{-ande}, 'one who'. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مساوی} (mosâvi)}{مساوی (mosâvi)}]{\fa{مساوی} (mosâvi) — equal; level (a draw)}

\label{lesson:FA-C513-mosavi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a point, then the Persian for a loser.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مساوی}}
\textbf{\fa{مساوی}} (\emph{mosâvi}) — \textquotedblleft{}equal; level (a draw)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بازی} \fa{دیشب} \fa{یک} \fa{یک} \fa{مساوی} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bâzi-ye dishab yek yek mosâvi shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Last night's match was a one-all draw.
\end{quote}

\emph{mosâvi shodan} — to end level. In sums, \emph{mosâvi} is 'equals'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mosâvi} is a loan, usually traced to Arabic \emph{musāwī}, 'equal'. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رکورد} (rekord)}{رکورد (rekord)}]{\fa{رکورد} (rekord) — a best result, a record}

\label{lesson:FA-C513-rekord}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a loser, then the Persian for equal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رکورد}}
\textbf{\fa{رکورد}} (\emph{rekord}) — \textquotedblleft{}a best result, a record\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{رکورد} \fa{مدرسه} \fa{را} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u rekord-e madrese râ dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She holds the school record.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{rekordhâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rekord} is a modern loan, usually traced to English \emph{record}. EtymDB has no entry for the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رکورد} \fa{زدن} (rekord zadan)}{رکورد زدن (rekord zadan)}]{\fa{رکورد} \fa{زدن} (rekord zadan) — to set a new best, to break a record}

\label{lesson:FA-C513-rekord-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for equal, then the Persian for a best result.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رکورد} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{رکورد} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{rekord zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to set a new best, to break a record\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{مسابقه} \fa{شنا} \fa{رکورد} \fa{زد}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\emph{rekord} + \emph{zadan} 'to strike'; present stem \emph{zan-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rekord zadan} joins \emph{rekord}, a loan usually traced to English \emph{record}, and inherited \emph{zadan}, 'to strike'.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گل} \fa{زدن} (gol zadan)}{گل زدن (gol zadan)}]{\fa{گل} \fa{زدن} (gol zadan) — to score a goal}

\label{lesson:FA-C513-gol-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a best result, then the Persian for to set a new best.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گل} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{گل} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{gol zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to score a goal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{دقیقه} \fa{آخر} \fa{گل} \fa{زد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u dar daqiqe-ye âkhar gol zad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He scored in the last minute.
\end{quote}

This \emph{gol} 'goal' is spelled like \emph{gol} 'flower'; + \emph{zadan} 'to strike'.

\begin{cousinweb}
This \emph{gol} was borrowed from English \emph{goal} (EtymDB); it only looks like native \emph{gol}, 'flower'. \emph{zadan}, 'to strike', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
